summary.text: 茶 names the tea plant and its prepared drink. Its written form is linked to 荼, an earlier graph analyzed with a plant-category element and a sound element; the exact graphic transition is uncertain.

formation.text: 茶 is a later graphic form linked to 荼. In the earlier graph, 艸 marks a plant category and 余 supplies a sound cue. This analysis does not assign separate meanings to every stroke of 茶.

components.text: In 荼, 艸 marks the plant category. This analysis belongs to 荼; it does not make every stroke of 茶 a meaningful component.
In 荼, 余 is analyzed as the phonetic element. In Zhengzhang’s reconstruction, its reading is compatible with 茶’s, but this does not establish 余’s original referent.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstruction, 余 is *la and 茶 is *rlaː, a plausible historical sound comparison. Their modern Mandarin readings, yú and chá, differ.

components.text: 茶 is linked to 荼 as a later graphic form. Medieval spellings varied, and accounts differ on whether 茶 began as an independent replacement, leaving the precise relationship and timing uncertain.

history.text: A seal-script-style rendering shows 荼, the earlier graph linked to 茶. It is a modern redraw, not an artifact or a dated witness to when 茶 emerged.
茶 is described as a later form related to 荼, but medieval spelling variation leaves its emergence as a distinct graph uncertain. Proposed Han forms and readings are also disputed or qualified.

uncertainties.text: The exact graphic path and date at which 茶 became distinct remain unsettled. Han uses of 荼 may refer to tea, but that reading is disputed; an older Shijing use is associated with a bitter plant whose exact species is uncertain.

Proposals for the spoken word’s deeper origin include borrowing from Loloish or Austroasiatic sources and development from 荼, ‘bitter plant’. The source language and borrowing pathway remain unresolved; these proposals concern the spoken word, not the graph’s formation.

senses.period: Tang period attested; earlier date unresolved
senses.text: 茶 is recorded for the tea plant. A Tang text describes tea as a fine southern tree, but the earliest date of this sense is unsettled.
Tang-period sources use 茶 for prepared tea. Proposed Han references written with 荼 remain disputed as evidence for this sense.

senses.gloss: infusion made from ingredients other than tea leaves
senses.text: 茶 is also recorded for brewed drinks made with other ingredients; the start of this use is undated.
A Ming example uses 茶 as a verb meaning ‘drink’; how this use developed from the noun is not established.
茶 is recorded as a metonym for betrothal gifts associated with tea; when this use began is undated.
茶 commonly names tea, including the plant and its prepared drink.

developments.text: The name for the tea plant is also used for the prepared drink. Both senses are attested, but their precise chronology is not established here.
The name extends to some other brewed drinks, though the timing is unspecified.
A Ming example records the verb ‘drink’, but the evidence does not explain how it developed from the noun.
The betrothal-gift use is recorded as a metonym associated with tea; its development and chronology are unspecified.

limitations.text: The Han 荼 passages are candidates, not uncontested evidence for an early tea sense. These senses do not identify the earliest historical use.
Competing proposals for the spoken word’s deeper origin remain unresolved; no source language or borrowing direction can be preferred.
